lines: A polyphonic wavefolder that scales and shifts the input before folding it, with a triangular fold and a sine fold
Chooses the fold: triangular reflects the signal back each time it passes a fold point, sinusoidal passes it through a sine function
Multiplies the input before folding, 1 to 10, so the signal crosses more fold points the further clockwise it goes
Attenuates the DEPTH input; at maximum, 10V there adds 40 to the folding depth on the unipolar setting, and 5V adds 40 on bipolar
Sets the range read at the DEPTH input: unipolar for 0-10V, bipolar for -5V to 5V
Shifts the scaled signal before folding, -2.5 to 2.5, moving it across the fold points
Attenuates the OFFSET input; at maximum, 10V there adds 20 to the folding offset on the unipolar setting, and 5V adds 20 on bipolar
Sets the range read at the OFFSET input: unipolar for 0-10V, bipolar for -5V to 5V
The signal to be folded, read as full scale at 5V; the number of channels here sets the number of channels at OUT
Adds to the folding depth set by Depth, through its own attenuator
Adds to the folding offset set by Offset, through its own attenuator
The folded signal, -5V to 5V
A sine LFO with a wavefolder on it: the folder shapes an external signal, or the built-in sine when nothing is patched in
Sets the rate of the built-in sine, 0.01Hz to 5Hz, and becomes a multiplier of the rate measured at SYNC while a cable is patched there
Chooses the fold: triangular reflects the signal back each time it passes a fold point, sinusoidal passes it through a sine function
Multiplies the signal before folding, 1 to 10, so it crosses more fold points the further clockwise it goes
Shifts the signal before folding, -2.5 to 2.5, moving it across the fold points
Sets the range read at the input jack: unipolar subtracts 5V first, treating 0-10V as centred on 5V, bipolar takes -5V to 5V unchanged
Sets the range of both outputs: unipolar gives 0-10V, bipolar gives -5V to 5V
The signal to be folded; with nothing patched here the fold is skipped and OUT carries the built-in sine unchanged, despite the tooltip calling this jack normalled to the LFO
A rising edge above 2V restarts the built-in sine and sets its rate from the time between edges, which LFO Freq then multiplies
The folded input signal, or the built-in sine with no folding applied when nothing is patched to the input jack
The built-in sine after folding, folded whatever is patched to the input jack
ACLFold.notes: Params 1, 2, 4, 6 and 10 are declared in the enum as reserved and have no widget, so they cannot be clicked. Output index 1 is the upper jack printed OUT and index 0 the lower jack printed LFO, the reverse of the index order. OUT is given no family because what it carries changes with whether the input jack is patched: the folded external signal, or the built-in sine with no folding.
